title: The Usual Suspects
events_chronological: Years earlier in Turkey, Hungarian gangsters hold Keyser Soze's family hostage, and he kills his own wife and children and then everyone connected to the men, and disappears into legend.
Five criminals - Keaton, McManus, Fenster, Hockney and Verbal Kint - are pulled into a truck-hijacking lineup in New York and held overnight in the same cell.
In the cell they plan revenge on the NYPD's "taxi service", a ring of corrupt officers escorting smugglers through the city.
The crew ambush the taxi service, and the ensuing scandal tears the department apart.
Keaton's lawyer and lover Edie Finneran gets them to Los Angeles, where McManus's contact Redfoot buys the stolen jewels.
Redfoot puts them on to a jeweller who turns out to be a Hungarian carrying heroin, and the crew realise they are being steered.
The lawyer Kobayashi appears, says he acts for Keyser Soze, tells each man he has unknowingly stolen from Soze, and orders them to destroy a boatload of his rivals' cocaine.
Fenster runs and is found shot dead on a beach.
The crew try to kill Kobayashi in his office and back off when he reveals he is holding Edie Finneran.
On the night of the raid the four survivors board the Hungarian boat in San Pedro harbour.
Hockney and McManus are killed below decks, and there is no cocaine anywhere on the ship.
Keaton is shot by a figure on deck while Verbal watches from the dockside, and the boat goes up in flames.
Customs agent Dave Kujan interrogates Verbal in a borrowed police office in San Pedro, pressing him to give up Keaton.
A burned Hungarian survivor tells the FBI from his hospital bed that Keyser Soze was on the boat, and begins describing him to a sketch artist.
Verbal, granted immunity, tells Kujan that Keaton was Soze all along, collects his belongings and walks out of the station.
Kujan realises that Verbal improvised the entire story from the noticeboard behind the desk and the maker's name on the bottom of a coffee cup.
Verbal's limp and his crippled hand straighten out as he walks down the street, and Kobayashi collects him in a waiting car.
The faxed sketch finishes printing, and the face on it is Verbal Kint's.
syuzhet_notes: Told-order bullet 1 is a flash-forward to the night of the raid, which the film only catches up with at told-order bullets 13-14. Everything from bullet 3 to bullet 14 is Verbal's narration, a long flashback nested inside the interrogation of bullet 2, and bullet 9 is a flashback within that flashback, reaching years further back into the Soze legend. The final bullets reveal the whole structure was improvised.
fabula_notes: Verbal is an unreliable narrator, so most of this chronology is his invention rather than the story world's; the ordering follows the account he gives, which the closing bullets expose as assembled on the spot from objects in the office. The Turkish massacre is delivered as legend rather than witnessed, and the identity of the man who shoots Keaton is left for the audience to infer.
